lines.t: Lord, I know how to write the chorus.
I know where Your name should go.
But when the speakers stop—
I don't know how to be alone with You.
That's what I haven't said.
Why do I breathe when the verdict goes quiet?
Why does relief feel like something I'm hiding?
Why do I smile, then examine the smile,
Like maybe being happy means I'm living in denial?
Wake up, court's in session again,
Judge in my skull with a list and a pen.
Before my feet land, I'm defending my worth;
How am I guilty before I've done work?
Read another page, try to make something happen,
Check for a feeling, get caught in the checking.
Was that sincere? Did I mean that prayer?
Say it again—maybe love will appear.
I'm bored and ashamed that I'm bored with the holy.
Surrounded by words, still feeling so lonely.
I say You have spoken, but still I feel far;
I don't know what to do with this ache in my heart.
I don't want another line that sounds right.
I want to stop lying about tonight.
If all I can bring is the truth of this room,
Can this be the place where I start seeking You?
YahuShua, here's what I've got:
An anxious mind and a heart tied in knots.
I don't feel close. I won't pretend.
I need more than another vow I can't defend.
Teach me the difference between turning from wrong
And dragging my name through the dirt all night long.
I want to come without staging the scene—
No more pretending I'm better than me.
I made every morning a spiritual trial,
Couldn't just live without checking the file.
Turned every silence into proof You withdrew,
Then blamed myself harder to get back to You.
But I can't make love by increasing the pressure,
Can't turn my grief into proof that I'm better.
Can't keep measuring every breath that I take
And call every moment of rest a mistake.
Still, I did harm. I won't hide that in sadness.
My pain doesn't cancel the need to change habits.
If I spoke cruelly, I'll name what I said;
Won't make them comfort my guilt instead.
If I broke trust, I can't pray them compliant.
If I need help, I can quit acting giant.
Tell someone plainly: “I'm not doing well.”
No polished-up testimony. Just tell.
YahuShua, here's what I've got:
An anxious mind and a heart tied in knots.
I don't feel close. I won't pretend.
I need more than another vow I can't defend.
Teach me the difference between turning from wrong
And dragging my name through the dirt all night long.
I want to come without staging the scene—
No more pretending I'm better than me.
I don't know You the way I keep saying.
Sometimes I'm scared while everyone is praying.
Sometimes I want to close the book
Before I find another reason I can't look up.
I miss enjoying an ordinary day.
I miss a laugh I don't interrogate.
I miss my children getting all of my attention
Without my mind rehearsing my next confession.
I don't want to use freedom to excuse what hurts them.
I don't want to use faith to keep myself hurting.
I want to learn what honest love requires—
Not keep proving I'm sincere by staying tired.
Tonight, no promise to rebuild my whole life.
One honest prayer without forcing it twice.
One specific wrong I can own and repair.
One person I trust who can know how I fare.
Tomorrow, sit down with the child in the room.
Listen without turning the moment into proof.
Let kindness be kindness, not points on a board.
Let my apology land without asking for reward.
Find someone qualified to hear this anxiety,
Someone who won't use my faith to frighten me.
Let getting support be a step I can take,
Not another secret I carry in shame.
And when I read, let me actually listen—
Not hunt for a sentence to feed the prosecution.
When I don't understand, let the question stay open.
I don't need to counterfeit certainty or devotion.
YahuShua, here's what I've got:
Not the clean ending I thought that You'd want.
Still some fear. Still some doubt.
But tonight I let the honest words come out.
I can face what I've done without becoming the wrong.
I can ask for help without dressing it in song.
If all I can offer is an unfinished plea,
Here is the man I've been frightened to let You see.
No victory speech.
No borrowed fire.
Just this:
Lord, I don't want to fake knowing You.
I want to begin honestly.
